questions.q: Why doesn't a plain Kubernetes Deployment fit a multi-node PyTorch training run?
options: Deployments cannot request GPU resources at all
Deployments keep identical, interchangeable replicas with no concept of a rank-0 master or cross-pod coordination
Deployments can only run one Pod at a time
Deployments are deprecated in current Kubernetes versions
questions.explain: A Deployment's replicas are interchangeable by design. Training needs a distinguished rank-0 (Master) and coordinated startup across all ranks, which a Deployment has no concept of.

questions.q: In a PyTorchJob spec, what does the Master replica group represent?
options: A separate monitoring sidecar container
Rank 0 of the distributed job, typically the single pod responsible for coordination and checkpoint writes
A backup copy of the Worker replicas for failover
The Kubernetes control plane node running the scheduler
questions.explain: The Master replica (always replicas: 1) is rank 0 — the process torchrun treats as the coordination point, and in Solara's setup, the one that writes checkpoints.

questions.q: Which four environment variables does torchrun require before it can call init_process_group, and who sets them in a PyTorchJob?
options: CPU_COUNT, MEM_LIMIT, GPU_TYPE, NODE_NAME — set manually by the user in each container
RANK, WORLD_SIZE, MASTER_ADDR, MASTER_PORT — injected automatically by the Kubeflow Training Operator
NAMESPACE, POD_NAME, SERVICE_NAME, CLUSTER_ID — set by kubelet at pod creation
IMAGE_TAG, REPLICA_TYPE, RESTART_COUNT, JOB_NAME — set by the container runtime
questions.explain: The Training Operator derives the Master's Service DNS name and each replica's rank/world size, injecting MASTER_ADDR, MASTER_PORT, RANK, and WORLD_SIZE into every Pod automatically.

questions.q: Solara's PyTorchJob has 1 Master replica and 63 Worker replicas, each requesting nvidia.com/gpu: 8. How many GPUs does the job use in total?
options: 64 GPUs
63 GPUs
512 GPUs
8 GPUs
questions.explain: 64 total replicas (1 Master + 63 Workers) × 8 GPUs each = 512 GPUs, the full solara-train cluster.

questions.q: A Worker Pod in the PyTorchJob exits with a non-zero code and its restartPolicy is OnFailure. What happens first?
options: The entire PyTorchJob is immediately marked Failed with no retry
The operator restarts just that Pod; the job only moves to Failed if retries are exhausted
Kubernetes deletes the whole namespace
Nothing — restartPolicy only applies to Deployments, not PyTorchJobs
questions.explain: The Training Operator honors restartPolicy per replica: a failing Worker gets restarted individually first, and the job is only marked Failed once retries are exhausted.
